excerpt: Over the years, our Inspection and Metrology products for the semiconductor industry included the Falcon, Condor, Gannet and Eagle products lines. As of today, we produce and sell the Eagle platform, the Hawk platform and the MicroProf platform, and have phased out all other models. Hawk | Launched on February 2025, this brand-new product family – the Hawk – a new cutting-edge platform is engineered for cutting edge advanced packaging: Chiplets, HBM and Hybrid Bonding.
scope_note: COMPARATOR ROW. Camtek's own description of its newest platform (launched Feb 2025) as engineered for 'cutting edge advanced packaging: Chiplets, HBM and Hybrid Bonding' -- a capability/design claim, not a production or order claim: no shipment, order or revenue figure is attached to Hawk specifically anywhere in this filing. Filed at multi_equipment because Hawk combines inspection and metrology on one platform (see platform record). Chiplets and Hybrid Bonding are named in the same sentence but are not separately registrable application_ids in this atlas (only tsv, advanced_packaging and hbm exist); recorded in words here rather than invented as links.
notes: W13 RECORDS REVIEW (accept) by claude_w13_records_verifier: Confirmed against camtek_20f_fy2025 p.1: Hawk "is engineered for cutting edge advanced packaging: Chiplets, HBM and Hybrid Bonding" matches verbatim, with HBM named explicitly (not inferred from an adjacent sentence). link_kind supplier_capability correct (design/engineering-purpose claim; launched Feb 2025, no shipment/revenue figure attached specifically). Chiplets and Hybrid Bonding correctly left unregistered as separate links since they are not valid application_ids in this atlas.

excerpt: EagleT-AP / Plus | The Eagle-AP system family addresses the fast-growing advanced packaging market using state of the art technologies, both software and hardware, that deliver superior 2D and 3D inspection and metrology capabilities on the same platform. The EagleT-AP metrology capabilities support the wide spectrum of bump sizes and all bump types, including copper pillars, micro-bumps, solder and gold bumps, meeting the advanced packaging market requirements, including measurement of bumps down to 2µm (microns) and providing high throughput.
scope_note: COMPARATOR ROW. Current platform explicitly positioned for the advanced-packaging bump market (copper pillar, micro-bump, solder, gold bump; down to 2 micron). Capability/design claim, not a production or order claim -- no shipment or revenue figure attached to EagleT-AP specifically. No HBM-specific wording, so registered against advanced_packaging generically rather than hbm.

excerpt: Approximately 50% of our revenues are generated from products supporting the production of artificial intelligence (“AI”) applications, and significant portion of our growth expected in the coming few years is derived from such products. We have experienced increased demand for inspection and metrology systems as customers invest in equipment supporting the production of AI related products, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced packaging.
scope_note: COMPARATOR ROW carrying Camtek's one published AI/HBM/advanced-packaging revenue EXPOSURE figure (company-wide, undifferentiated between HBM and other AI-related or advanced-packaging demand): 'Approximately 50% of our revenues are generated from products supporting the production of...AI...applications...including high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced packaging.' Registered as production_claim (a revenue-driver statement) at the entity level (no single platform named) and at multi_equipment (the basket spans whichever inspection and metrology tools serve this end-market mix). The matching quantified observation is CAMTEK-AI-REVSHARE-2025 (revenue_share, ~50%, camtek_ai_related_products scope). Do not read this as an HBM-specific revenue split: HBM is one of several named AI-related products ('including...HBM and advanced packaging'), not isolated from the 50%.
notes: W13 RECORDS REVIEW (accept) by claude_w13_records_verifier: Confirmed against camtek_20f_fy2025 p.1: "Approximately 50% of our revenues are generated from products supporting the production of...AI...applications...including high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced packaging" matches verbatim, with HBM named by name (not inferred from an adjacent sentence). link_kind production_claim correct ('are generated' is present-tense realized revenue, not a booking or forecast). application_id hbm is defensible since HBM is explicitly named, though this is genuinely the WEAKEST form of hbm-tagged evidence in the batch: the 50% figure is an undifferentiated company-wide AI-exposure estimate that bundles HBM with 'advanced packaging' and other unnamed AI-related products without any HBM-specific split, and the scope_note is honest about this ('do not read this as an HBM-specific revenue split'). No taxonomy rule is broken, so no correction is made, but flagged in the handback report as the weakest HBM evidence identified in this review.
